_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 1 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 2 Parts of a Plant. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in order (a seed wakes up; roots and stem; leaves and flower; light and water; tools and measuring, here as two chapters), in the lesson's own words: its seed demo (ART.scene plant 0-2), its tap figure (ART.figure plant, one part named at a time), its light test (ART.pots with darkB, by the window and in the cupboard), its tools and its cubes.
title: Parts of a Plant
subtitle: Grade 1 Science
objectives: Recognise and name the major parts of familiar flowering plants (limited to roots, leaves, stems and flowers).
Know that plants need light and water to survive.
Follow instructions safely when doing practical work.

beats.say: Look at a plant. It has four main parts.
Each part does a different job. The plant needs all four.
A new plant grows from a seed. It looks dead, but it is not.
A tiny baby plant, and food for it, are packed inside.
Give it water and warmth, and it wakes up.
A root pushes down first. It is hidden in the soil.
Then a shoot pushes up, out of the soil, towards the light.
Here is the whole plant. Let us start at the bottom.
These are the roots. They hold the plant steady in the soil.
The roots drink up water from the soil, like straws.
This is the stem, the tall stalk. It holds the plant up.
The stem carries the water up, from the roots to every part.
These are the leaves. They are flat and green.
Leaves catch sunlight and use it to make the plant's food.
A plant makes its own food, in its leaves. It does not eat soil.
This is the flower. It is the colourful part at the top.
The flower makes seeds, so there can be new plants next year.
The whole thing is a plant. The flower is only one part.
A plant needs water and light to stay alive.
Take away the water, and the plant droops.
Today you will test the light, with two plants.
One goes by the window. One goes in a dark cupboard.
Both get water. Only one thing is different: the light.
In the dark, the plant goes pale and thin. Water is not enough.
Scientists use tools. A magnifying glass helps you look closely.
Hold it near your eye, and move the leaf closer.
Never point it at the sun. It can burn.
Gloves keep soil off your hands. Wash your hands afterwards anyway.
A ruler or cubes can measure how tall a plant is.
Stack cubes beside it, one at a time. Stop when they reach the top.
Count them: one, two, three. The seedling is three cubes tall.
Roots drink, the stem carries, leaves make food, the flower makes seeds.
Plants need light and water. Both.
Scientists use tools safely, and you can measure a plant in cubes.
